findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

During this inspection the PIC was unable to show a verifiable manner in which the employees are notified of their responsibility to report potential foodborne illnesses and symptoms. A 10 day follow up lands on a Saturday. The scheduled follow up will be conducted on the following Monday. A blank copy of the Sangamon County Reporting Agreement will be given with the hand delivered report.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11.

The cooler in the back-stock area of the facility has mold growth observed on the cardboard at the bottom as well as on the edges of the door glass. The PIC was notified and instructed to clean and maintain clean moving forward. Ensure that all food related equipment is maintained in a clean state at all times.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. 

The mops in the back of the facility are observed stored with the heads in soiled water or pooled up in the bottom of mop buckets. Between uses these items should be stored so that the bristles are able to hang and drip dry effectively. The situation was discussed with the PIC and they’re instructed to handguns the bristles over the ringer so that the bristles could drip dry.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  

On arrival PIC was unable to show verification of employees responsibility to report foodborne illnesses. Reporting agreements were given during this inspection and filled out to correct.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. 

No vomit or diarrheal clean up procedures are available for inspector observation during this inspection. The procedure given out by SCDPH was given during this inspection to correct.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

The bathroom hand sink is without paper towels during this inspection. Paper towels were supplied to correct the violation.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
3-202.15: FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. 

Multiple cans are observed on the shelves with significant dents and dents along the seams. PIC was consulted and the cans discarded to correct the violation. It was suggested to have a conversation with the stockers about setting aside damaged cans for credit/discard.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment: Floors throughout the facility appear to be dirty, especially (but not limited to) around the drinks coolers at the front of the store, at the back of the store near the freezers, and spills in at least one aisle. Ref. 6-501.12 [C]

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment: Several containers of grapes observed with their contents molded together. Soft/rotten potatoes and onions observed in the display along with bags of moldy potatoes. CORRECTED- Rotten/moldy foods voluntarily discarded. Ref. 3-101.11 [P]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment: Flies and gnats observed around the produce area. Eliminate pests. Remove moldy/rotten produce and clean the area to eliminate harborage conditions. Ref. 6-501.111 [C]

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment: Soil accumulation observed in the produce displays, both dry (potatoes, onions, etc) and cold (berries, cauliflower, etc). Clean to prevent contamination of foods. Ref. 3-305.11 [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment: Floors throughout the facility observed to be dirty, with soil accumulation observed along the bottoms of coolers and in corners. Moisture observed around the bottoms of the produce cooler and beverage coolers. Spills in several aisles are visible. Clean floors. Ref. 6-501.12 [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Handwashing sink in the women's restroom did not provide hot water after a reasonable amount of time (longer than someone would likely wait to wash their hands). Ensure hot water is available to allow proper handwashing.
5-202.12: (A) HANDWASHING SINK shall be equipped to provide water of a temperature at least 100F through mixing valve.
